answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce token in a public vault before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent reviewers confirm fraud. A hollow identity is cheap to create, but it cannot earn influence without capital at risk; splitting into a garden of sybils multiplies the bonds required, while colluding accounts expose more stake to coordinated slashing. The defense raises the attacker’s cost, though it does not prove identities are unique.
